explanation: The TV series began in 1966, with its burning-fuse titles and Lalo Schifrin's theme. Tom Cruise's first film version followed 30 years later, in 1996.

claims.text: The TV series Mission: Impossible was first broadcast in 1966.
The first Mission: Impossible film, starring Tom Cruise, was released in 1996.
Lalo Schifrin composed the Mission: Impossible theme for the TV series.
The TV series' title sequence shows a burning fuse.

writerNotes: Self-check 9.3. Lint: clean. Claims: every claim listed, risk at or above the C26 floor and raised where a detail is easy to get wrong; the schema's riskReason list has no 'only' or 'counterintuitive', so such claims carry the nearest listed reason. Datasets: no pinned dataset covers film or TV facts, so every high-risk claim here needs checker evidence from the web. Rival test: Players who know only the film series pick the cinema side; the TV original came 30 years earlier. Volatility: evergreen; no time words; nothing depends on events after mid-2026. Regional: both the series and the films were shown worldwide. Style: Oxford spelling, straight single quotes, plain hyphens, explanation of 25 words. Myths: claims screened against myths.json; no claim resembles a listed myth. Mystery and encore: not applicable to a practice item. Doubts: none beyond the high-risk claims flagged for external evidence.

editor.reason: Both checks pass, but high-risk claims c1 and c2 rest on knowledge only: neither checker could search (the shared search budget was spent) and no pinned dataset covers film, so §9.9 rule 3 cannot pass.
